title: The Prophet's intercession
hook: the Prophet ﷺ will intercede for his community (Bukhari)

segments.voice: Yesterday, sirat, the bridge, and your line: cross with light. Which light did you choose: prayer, a gift, or patience? Today, on that same long Day, someone speaks up for others. Day one thousand two hundred sixty-one.

The plain is crowded and the waiting is long, and the people do what people do when things are hard. They look for someone to speak for them. A hadith in Sahih al-Bukhari, narrated by Anas, tells it as a search. They go to Adam: will you ask your Lord for us? Not me, he says, and sends them on. To Noah. Not me. To Abraham. To Moses. To Jesus. Each one, gently, says: not me, go to another. And the last one sends them to the Prophet Muhammad, peace be upon him. Today, the one who says yes.
screen: `A SEARCH ACROSS THE PLAIN.` → `ADAM, NOAH, ABRAHAM, MOSES, JESUS.` → `NOT ME. GO TO ANOTHER.`

segments.voice: The word is shafa'ah, intercession: speaking to someone on another's behalf. In the hadith, the Prophet goes, and the first thing he does is not speak. He falls down in prostration before his Lord, and stays there. Then he is told: raise your head; ask, and you will be given; intercede, and your intercession will be accepted. Then, the hadith says, he intercedes. Two things hold this teaching in place. First, the Qur'an is clear that intercession is never a way around Allah. In the Throne Verse, Pickthall's translation asks: "Who is he that intercedeth with Him save by His leave?" Nobody speaks on the Day unless permitted. The Prophet's intercession is a permission, granted. Second, it was saved. Another hadith in Bukhari has him say that every prophet has one prayer sure to be answered, and he wanted to keep his back, as intercession for his community on the Day of Resurrection. Kept, for the Day. Theologians from the part we just finished discussed who it reaches. Sunni theologians, as they're remembered, affirmed that it can reach believers who sinned gravely, and the Mu'tazilah held a narrower view. The hadith also name a way to ask for it. A hadith in Sahih Muslim says that whoever sends one blessing on the Prophet, Allah sends ten on them; and that whoever, after the call to prayer, asks Allah to grant him the station called al-wasilah, his intercession becomes due for that person. So the blessing travels both directions. The community sends salawat to him, and the hope is that he speaks for them.
screen: `NOT SPEECH FIRST: PROSTRATION.` · `SAVE BY HIS LEAVE.` · `ONE PRAYER, KEPT FOR THE DAY.` · then, large: `BLESSING SENT, INTERCESSION HOPED FOR.`

segments.voice: The practice: send salawat. If you're Muslim, settle and breathe, and say the familiar words slowly, a few times, in Arabic or in English: allahumma salli 'ala Muhammad, O Allah, send blessings on Muhammad. Let each one be unhurried. If you're not Muslim, you can sit with the shape of the idea instead. Bring to mind someone who has spoken up for you, once, when you couldn't speak for yourself. A parent, a teacher, a friend in a hard meeting. Hold them in mind, and wish them well. The bell holds the time.
Shafa'ah. Intercession: speaking for another, only by Allah's leave; the Prophet's, Muslims hold, kept for his community on the Day. Today's word.
Your line: he will intercede. Today, speak up once for someone who isn't in the room to speak for themselves. Tomorrow, the pool. Day one thousand two hundred sixty-one.

howItsDone: Muslims send blessings on the Prophet, salawat, in their prayers and when his name is mentioned, and after the call to prayer they may ask Allah to grant him al-wasilah, hoping for his intercession on the Day of Resurrection.

original.note: Arabic: intercession, speaking on another's behalf.

trapdoor: what you thought: intercession means someone gets a person off the hook.
what it means: speaking for others on the Day, only by Allah's leave; the Prophet's, Muslims hold, is kept for his community.
what a scholar hears: the search from Adam to Jesus in Anas's hadith, the prayer kept back, and the theologians' debate over whom it reaches.

sources.ref: Sahih al-Bukhari 4476 (Anas: the people go from prophet to prophet)
Sahih al-Bukhari 6304 (every prophet's one answered prayer; his kept for intercession)
Sahih Muslim 384 (one blessing, ten; al-wasilah and intercession)

notes: Bukhari 4476 and 6304, Muslim 384: confirm numbers and paraphrase.
Sunni affirmation of intercession for grave sinners vs a narrower Mu'tazili view: confirm that the summary is fair to both.
Practice: 'allahumma salli 'ala Muhammad' offered as a familiar formula of salawat, not a new prayer; confirm transliteration.

Editor pass: Bukhari 6304 doesn't say every other prophet used his prayer in his lifetime, and 'for people he would never meet' isn't in the text; both cut, and the kept prayer is now paraphrased closer to 6304.
The hadith's list of prophets (Adam to Jesus) is told as the hadith tells it; no comparison intended.
